function.name: get_weather_forecast
function.description: Retrieves the weather forecast for a specified location and date range. The forecast includes temperature, precipitation, and wind speed. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which the weather forecast is requested, in the format of 'City, Country' (e.g., 'London, UK').

start_date.description: The start date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-01').

end_date.description: The end date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-07').

units.description: The unit system in which to return the weather forecast data.

include_details.description: Specifies whether to include detailed forecast information such as humidity and visibility.

### How Turbonomic Helps Unilever Leverage AI for Multi‑Cloud Observability | What Turbonomic Provides | Why It Matters for Unilever | How It Works | |--------------------------|-----------------------------|--------------| | **Unified, AI‑driven Resource Optimization** | Unilever runs workloads across GCP, AWS, Azure, and private clouds. Turbonomic continuously collects telemetry from all environments and applies machine‑learning models to predict demand, detect inefficiencies, and recommend actions. | • Real‑time monitoring of CPU, memory, I/O, network, and storage usage.
• Predictive analytics that forecast future capacity needs based on historical trends and upcoming events (e.g., seasonal campaigns).
• Automated remediation (e.g., right‑size VMs, move workloads, adjust autoscaling thresholds). | | **Cross‑Cloud Cost Visibility & Control** | Managing spend across multiple providers is complex. Turbonomic aggregates cost data, normalizes pricing models, and shows where money is being spent versus where savings can be realized. | • Pulls billing APIs from GCP Billing, AWS Cost Explorer, Azure Cost Management.
• Normalizes units (USD, EUR) and currency conversion.
• Generates actionable reports (e.g., “$X saved by moving workload Y from AWS to GCP”). | | **Policy‑Based Governance** | Unilever has strict compliance, security, and sustainability policies. Turbonomic lets you encode those rules into a single policy engine that spans all clouds. | • Define policies (e.g., “No public IPs on production workloads”, “Maximum 30% of resources on spot instances”).
• Turbonomic enforces them automatically, generating alerts or taking corrective action. | | **Performance & SLA Assurance** | Retail and FMCG operations require high availability and low latency. Turbonomic monitors SLAs and ensures they’re met while optimizing costs. | • Monitors application metrics (latency, error rates) via integrations with Prometheus, Datadog, New Relic, etc.
• Uses AI to balance load across regions or providers to meet SLA targets. | | **Integrated Incident Response** | When something goes wrong, Turbonomic can trigger incident tickets, run playbooks, or even roll back changes. | • Integrates with PagerDuty, ServiceNow, Slack, Teams.
• Automates root‑cause analysis by correlating infrastructure telemetry with application logs. | #### Key Benefits for Unilever 1. **Single Pane of Glass** – One dashboard for all clouds, eliminating the need to switch between GCP Console, AWS Management Console, Azure Portal, etc. 2. **Cost Savings** – Typical savings reported by enterprises using Turbonomic are 10–30 % of total cloud spend, achieved through rightsizing, reserved instance optimization, and workload placement. 3. **Operational Agility** – AI recommendations are delivered in seconds; Turbonomic can auto‑apply changes or provide “what‑if” simulations for human approval. 4. **Compliance & Sustainability** – Policies can enforce green‑IT goals (e.g., prioritize renewable‑energy‑powered regions) and regulatory requirements (GDPR, SOC 2). 5. **Reduced Manual Workload** – Engineers spend less time on capacity planning and more on innovation. --- ### Difference Between Turbonomic and Native Cloud Monitoring/Management Tools | Feature | Turbonomic | GCP Operations Suite (formerly Stackdriver) | AWS CloudWatch | Azure Monitor | |---------|------------|-------------------------------------------|----------------|---------------| | **Scope** | Cross‑cloud (multi‑provider + on‑prem) | Single‑provider (GCP only) | Single‑provider (AWS only) | Single‑provider (Azure only) | | **Primary Focus** | AI‑driven optimization & governance | Logging, monitoring, alerting | Metrics, logs, alarms | Metrics, logs, alerts | | **Optimization Engine** | Machine‑learning models that recommend actions (rightsizing, placement, scaling) | No built‑in optimization; relies on manual dashboards | No built‑in optimization; uses CloudWatch Alarms + Lambda scripts | No built‑in optimization; uses Azure Automation + Logic Apps | | **Cost Management** | Unified cost aggregation, predictive forecasting, policy‑based cost control | GCP Billing API integration; basic cost dashboards | AWS Cost Explorer, Budgets | Azure Cost Management + Advisor | | **Automation** | Policy‑based automation that can take corrective action automatically | Limited automation via Cloud Functions, Cloud Scheduler | Automation via CloudWatch Events + Lambda | Automation via Azure Logic Apps, Automation Accounts | | **Observability Depth** | Combines infrastructure telemetry, application performance, business KPIs, and cost data | Infrastructure metrics + logs + traces | Same but provider‑specific | Same but provider‑specific | | **Integration Ecosystem** | Connects to Prometheus, Datadog, New Relic, Splunk, PagerDuty, ServiceNow, etc. | Native GCP services; limited third‑party connectors | Native AWS services; limited third‑party connectors | Native Azure services; limited third‑party connectors | | **User Experience** | Unified UI, AI‑generated insights, “what‑if” simulation | Provider‑specific dashboards | Provider‑specific dashboards | Provider‑specific dashboards | | **Learning Curve** | Requires learning Turbonomic’s policy language and AI concepts | Familiar if already using GCP | Familiar if already using AWS | Familiar if already using Azure | #### Bottom Line - **Native tools** give you deep visibility *within* each provider and are great for provider‑specific troubleshooting and cost tracking. - **Turbonomic** adds a layer of *cross‑cloud intelligence*, turning raw telemetry into actionable decisions that span all your environments. It bridges gaps between cost, performance, and compliance, and automates many tasks that would otherwise require manual scripting or manual intervention. For Unilever, adopting Turbonomic means: - A single platform that understands the nuances of each cloud provider’s pricing and performance characteristics. - AI that can suggest moving a workload from an expensive region in AWS to a cheaper zone in GCP without compromising latency. - Policies that enforce corporate standards (e.g., “All production workloads must run on at least one dedicated host”) across all clouds. In short, Turbonomic turns the complexity of a multi‑cloud strategy into a set of clear, data‑driven actions—something native tools alone cannot deliver.
